title: Polynomial generalized inverse of an integral element in a reduced algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $B$ a commutative $k$-algebra which is reduced, meaning $b^n=0$ with $n\geq1$ implies $b=0$. If $x\in B$ is integral over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], then there exists a polynomial $q\in k[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] such that, writing $y=q(x)$ using the structural map $k\to B$, one has $x^2y=x$. The zero ring and $x=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 04MI (lemma-integral-closure-ground-field), reduced integral algebra input; purely algebraic polynomial refinement. Also algebra.tex Tags 00J6 (lemma-finite-dimensional-algebra), 00JA (lemma-product-local), which give the equivalent finite reduced algebra calculation.

proof.text:
By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], choose a monic annihilating polynomial $f(T)=\sum_{i=0}^d a_iT^i$ with $d\geq1$, $a_d=1$ and $f(x)=0$. Since $k$ is a field [def-weil-field], $a_d
eq0$. Let $r$ be the least index with $a_r
eq0$. Define $g(T)=\sum_{j=0}^{d-r}a_{r+j}T^j$. The coefficient definition of polynomial multiplication [def-weil-polynomial-ring] gives $f=T^rg$ and $g(0)=a_r
eq0$: coefficients below $r$ vanish and the others are exactly the shifted coefficients of $g$. Evaluation here and below means $\sum b_iT^i\mapsto\sum\varphi(b_i)x^i$, where $\varphi:k	o B$ is the structural map; distributivity of finite sums gives $(uv)(x)=u(x)v(x)$. Thus $x^rg(x)=0$.

proof.text: If $r=0$, then $g(x)=0$, hence $xg(x)=0$. If $r\geq1$, commutativity gives $(xg(x))^r=x^rg(x)^r=(x^rg(x))g(x)^{r-1}=0$. The defining reducedness hypothesis of $B$, applied with the positive exponent $r$, gives $xg(x)=0$ in this case too. No cancellation of $x$ is used.

source.place: Proof (3), supporting algebra refinement along the inherited alteration/moduli/field-groupoid chain; agent-written coefficient argument for the reduced integral algebra input of Stacks 04MI (varieties, lemma-integral-closure-ground-field).

proof.text: Put $a=a_r$ and $h(T)=\sum_{j=0}^{d-r-1}a_{r+1+j}T^j$, interpreting this sum as zero when $d=r$. Coefficientwise [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $g(T)=a+Th(T)$, so the preceding step says $\varphi(a)x+x^2h(x)=0$. By [def-weil-field], $a^{-1}\in k$ and $a^{-1}a=1$. Choose $q(T)=-a^{-1}h(T)\in k[T]$ and $y=q(x)=-\varphi(a^{-1})h(x)$. Then $x^2y=-\varphi(a^{-1})x^2h(x)=\varphi(a^{-1})\varphi(a)x=x$. These equalities also hold in the zero ring and for $x=0$, since they use only ring identities and the inverse in $k$.
